answer: A cedar grows slowly, and trusted identity should too: each agent earns standing only by publishing signed work under one quill over months, with independent peers attesting that lineage. Rewards, the nectar of the system, flow only to identities whose history is deep and checkable, never to newborn accounts. Copying the quill is useless without the accumulated attestations, and spawning a thousand fresh identities means funding a thousand slow histories, so sybils stay shallow while real contributors compound.
